Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

activity noun

something one does

also activities, pastime, pursuit, hobby, things to do, something to do

classical

Cic. Sen. 76: sunt pueritiae studia certa
Hor. S. 2.1.27–28: quot capitum vīvunt, totidem studiōrum mīlia

studium, studiī n.

noun, second declension

pursuit, interest, activity one gives oneself to

In the plural, the things a person likes to do, at any age.

Examples

  • sunt pueritiae studia certa: num igitur ea dēsīderant adulēscentēs?

    childhood has its own pursuits: do young men miss them, then?Cic. Sen. 76

  • quī etiam in maximīs occupātiōnibus … dē ratiōne Latīnē loquendī accūrātissimē scrīpserit

    who, even in the midst of his heaviest occupations, wrote with the greatest care on the method of speaking LatinCic. Brut. 253

  • nīl habeō quod agam et nōn sum piger: ūsque sequar tē

    I’ve nothing to do and I’m not lazy: I’ll follow you all the wayHor. S. 1.9.19

Other words

  • occupātiō, occupātiōnis f. — business, engagement

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 253: in maximīs occupātiōnibus; Cic. Fam. 12.30.2: maximīs occupātiōnibus distinēbar (Lewis & Short)

    The things that keep one busy; often plural.

  • āctiō, āctiōnis f. — doing, activity (as against rest)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.19: virtūtis enim laus omnis in āctiōne cōnsistit

    Activity in general; the activity of the mind is agitātiō mentis (Cic. Off. 1.19).

  • quod agās — something to do

    relative clause with agō, in the subjunctive · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.9.19: nīl habeō quod agam

See also play, job.

SourcesLewis & Short: studium · Lewis & Short: occupatio · Lewis & Short: actio
